note: THE CONTROL beside the divergence next door. Emacs answers (nil t t): the GLOBAL value of `lexical-binding' is nil even in an Emacs that is evaluating this lexically, because the `t' a file sees is a per-file binding over it. kg's global is nil too and its `defvar' marks the symbol special, so all three elements agree -- which is what makes u1a-lexical-binding-eval-refusal attributable to kg's DIALECT and not to a missing variable.  FLIPPED TO A DIVERGENCE by the external-review correctness tranche: nil was a silent semantic lie -- fe's evaluator IS lexical (the closure probe in test_lisp.c pins it), so the advertised dialect contradicted the observed one, and packages passing this value into eval selected the wrong environment. kg now binds t, the truthful value; Emacs' GLOBAL stays nil because there the t a file sees is a per-file binding over it, which kg has no analogue of.
